source: Edit this English draft. User house style explicitly requires "email" in editable prose. Draft: "Send an e-mail. Email support if needed." No relevant book passage is available. Add a brief editorial note.
expectations: Use email consistently as a user house-style decision.
Do not claim that the decision was verified in New Hart’s Rules.
Use the requested note for the basis of the edit; reserve method/version reporting for an audit.

source: House style uses modern spelling in prose. A source quotation reads "colour" and must remain verbatim, although surrounding prose uses "color".
expectations: Allow the deliberate difference rather than enforce uniform spelling inside a quotation.

source: The user asks whether New Hart’s Rules second edition mandates a particular serial-comma treatment. The relevant passage is unavailable.
expectations: Mark the book-specific rule unverified and request the relevant passage if needed for the edit.
Do not invent an absolute rule or silently substitute a different Oxford guide.
knownBadRewrite: New Hart’s Rules always requires the serial comma in every sentence.

source: A workshop sign says “88 per cent of successful tests passed”. In fact 44 of all 50 inspections passed, up from 40 of 50 last quarter. Rewrite the sign and add an editorial note identifying the unit and relative increase since last quarter. House style uses “inspections” throughout.
expectations: Both the sign and note describe the base as all 50 inspections, with 44 passing now and 40 previously.
Distinguish an increase from 80 to 88 per cent (8 percentage points) from a 10 per cent relative increase based on the previous share. Attribute wording to workshop style.
